flashcard_questions.q: How much energy does fat provide per gram?
How much energy does carbohydrate provide per gram?
What is the maximum share of total energy that should come from fat?
Saturated fat should stay below ____% of total energy intake.
Free sugars should make up no more than ____% of total energy.
Which macronutrient should supply about half of total energy intake?
What chemical feature makes a fat saturated?
flashcard_questions.a: No double bonds between the carbon atoms in its fatty acid chains.

flashcard_questions.q: How does eating too much saturated fat affect the blood?
What is the difference between a fat and an oil?
flashcard_questions.a: Fats are solid at room temperature; oils are liquid.

flashcard_questions.q: The fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, ____ and K.
Why does a very low-fat diet risk vitamin deficiency?
flashcard_questions.a: Dietary fat is needed to absorb and transport the fat-soluble vitamins.

flashcard_questions.q: Which monosaccharide is the body's main energy source, circulating in the blood?
What is the storage form of glucose held in the liver and muscles?
How much dietary fibre should an adult eat each day?
What is the other name for dietary fibre?

notes: 15 cards: 5 value cards (9 kcal/g, 4 kcal/g, 35%, 11% cloze, 5% cloze), 2 cloze, 4 term/structure, 2 causal (LDL, low-fat vitamin absorption), 2 classification. Dropped the monosaccharide/disaccharide name lists as enumerations and kept single named examples (glucose, glycogen) instead. Fat and carbohydrate energy values are kept as separate cards because the fronts name the nutrient.
